item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q023_homeodomain_heterogeneous_fold","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1p7jd_ (SUNID 94286) and d1ztra1 (SUNID 125655) share the Homeodomain family a.4.1.1 (SUNID 46690), the Homeodomain-like superfamily a.4.1, and even the Engrailed Homeodomain protein/species lineage. Thus common ancestry remains strongly justified at family strength; the hf flag does not erase sequence-based homology. However, d1ztra1 is explicitly a domain-level heterogeneous-fold exception: despite similar sequence and secondary-structure count, it adopts a different fold from the family exemplar. Therefore homology must not be converted into an assumption of identical topology, residue correspondence, packing, or conformation. d1ztra1 and d1p7jd_ should not be used as interchangeable structural templates without direct pairwise structural/topological validation; mutation and experimental-state effects also matter because both are annotated mutants and d1p7jd_ is complexed with NHE. Likewise, they should not be treated as redundant same-fold positives or leakage-prone interchangeable training examples: d1ztra1 must retain its hf exception label, or be separated/excluded when the target label is fold or geometry. Family membership alone also cannot transfer detailed binding effects or function; those require independent sequence, structural-alignment, and biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1p7jd_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1ztra1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/94286","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/125655","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46692","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1p7jd_/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ztra1/homology"]}]}
